engineVersionNotes: Locked at 1.18.27 for this delivery. The npm registry's latest at the time of the distribution check was 1.18.29, and every distribution fact below was read out of opencode-ai@1.18.29; nothing in that shape changed between the two. Raising the lock is a deliberate, separately verified step, not a side effect of this config.

distribution.notes: opencode-ai declares bin {"opencode": "./bin/opencode.exe"} and ships that file as a ~479-byte placeholder. Its postinstall.mjs resolves the real, Bun-compiled standalone executable (~172 MB) out of the platform-specific optional dependency for the host - opencode-windows-x64 on Windows x64, opencode-windows-x64-baseline when the CPU has no AVX2 - hard-links or copies it over bin/opencode.exe, and validates it with --version. There is no JS entry script anywhere in the package, so `node.exe <script> acp` cannot work against a real install; the launch target is the .exe itself. Both the opencode-ai copy and the platform package's own bin/opencode.exe are real executables, which is why both are probed.
distribution.windowsNativeSupportEvidence: opencode.ai/docs/ states "While OpenCode can run directly on Windows, we recommend using WSL for the best experience": native Windows runs, it is simply not the recommended environment. The distribution backs this up - a first-party Windows x64 executable is published and installed by default. See docs/engines/opencode.md.

acp.subcommandEvidence: opencode.ai/docs/acp/ documents `opencode acp` as a stdio JSON-RPC ACP agent with no further arguments. Exercised against the real 1.18.29 binary on Linux (initialize + session/new completed).

exe.wellKnownPathNotes: Order is npm's default global prefix first (%APPDATA%\npm), then the platform packages that back it, then a Node installed under Program Files with a machine-wide prefix, then a hand-placed install. A template whose ${VAR} is unset is skipped, never probed as a root-relative path. On a non-Windows host set PNP_OPENCODE_EXE_PATH to the opencode-linux-x64 binary; there is no POSIX well-known list because npm's prefix there is not fixed.

node.fallbackNotes: Only used by the explicitly opt-in node-script mode. When unresolved, falls back to process.execPath (the gateway's own node.exe).

executable.modeNotes: exe is the shipped default because it is the only mode that matches the real distribution. node-script is retained as an explicit opt-in (PNP_OPENCODE_EXECUTABLE_KIND=node-script plus PNP_OPENCODE_SCRIPT_PATH) for a repackaged or future JS-entry build; it has no well-known script paths because opencode-ai ships no script entry to point at. npm's global install also writes an opencode.cmd shim, which the shared ProcessHost rejects (shell:false, and on win32 the executable must end in .exe); the shim is never a launch target in either mode.

nativePermissionsNotes: OpenCode permits every operation by default. "ask" writes "permission": {"edit": "ask", "bash": "ask"} into the private config so the engine raises ACP session/request_permission and the gateway's policy layer gets to decide allow/ask/deny. "engine-default" leaves the block out entirely and the engine never asks. PNP_OPENCODE_NATIVE_PERMISSIONS overrides this field at load time (same two values; empty or unset means "use this file", anything else fails the load with ENGINE_CONFIG_INVALID), so a deployment or a smoke run can turn engine-side prompting on without editing a checked-in file.

redirect.notes: Every key here is set on the child process only, rooted under EngineOpenInput.nativeDataDirectory/opencode/<value>. The shared ProcessHost's baseEnvironment() otherwise inherits the gateway's real HOME/USERPROFILE/APPDATA/LOCALAPPDATA, which would point opencode at the operator's real profile. The private config is reached primarily through OPENCODE_CONFIG, a documented discovery step (opencode.ai/docs/config/) that names one exact file and does not depend on guessing a config home; these directory redirects still matter for data/cache writes, for skill discovery, and as a fallback mirror. The documented order is remote .well-known, global ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json, OPENCODE_CONFIG, project opencode.json, .opencode, OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT, managed %ProgramData%\opencode; XDG_CONFIG_HOME and %APPDATA% are not named in that document at all.

model.rationale: A real opencode 1.18.29 acp session on Linux returned a model-category session config option ({id:"model", category:"model", type:"select"}) whose currentValue was exactly the provider/model pinned in the private config, so both routes exist. "launch" stays the shipped default because it fails closed: the model is pinned in the private opencode.json's top-level `model` field (provider/model syntax) and any request for a different model is rejected before a prompt is sent (ENGINE_MODEL_SWITCH_UNSUPPORTED) instead of being silently answered by another model. Switch to "session-config" only when per-session switching is actually wanted; pack.ts already branches on this field.
